name: Símákonde
catalog_citation: Manus, Sophie. 2010. The Prosody of Símákonde Relative Clauses. ZAS Papers in Linguistics 53: 159-185 (Papers from the Workshop on Bantu Relative Clauses). Open-access PDF, zaspil.leibniz-zas.de article 388.
catalog_locator: sec. 3.1 'Stress', p.161 (also abstract p.159); examples (1) p.162
catalog_quote: Like other Makonde dialects and other Eastern and Southern Bantu languages (Hyman 2009), Símákonde has lost the historical Proto-Bantu vowel length contrast and now has a regular phrase-final stress rule, which causes a predictable lengthening of the penultimate syllable of every Prosodic Phrase. The penult lengthened by stress is bimoraic. ... Examples in (1) show penultimate lengthening in Símákonde. (1) a. kúlúúma 'to bite' b. kúlúmúúla 'to cut' c. kúlúmúláánga 'to cut into small pieces' d. kúlúmúlángííla 'to cut into small pieces for someone'
sweep_summary: Four title-keyword items for Makonde (mako1251, catalog 'phrasal' on Manus 2010). Read: (1) Liphola 1991 UNICAMP MA thesis — newly located and downloaded open from the UNICAMP Sophia repository (scanned PDF with text layer, saved); it separates predictable, optional pre-pausal penultimate lengthening (no length contrast) from 'acento de intensidade', which it equates with High tone and describes as variable in position; refines the catalog (confirms the pause-final penult lengthening, questions calling it stress). (2) Philippson 1991 thesis (already held by the project, copied into the folder): §3.9 and p. 358 n. 1 — Makonde has a demarcative accent realized as penultimate lengthening before absolute pause, no length contrast; confirms. Not read: (3) Liphola 1992 LASU proceedings — print only (OCLC 29617455), medium priority; (4) Liphola 2001 OSU dissertation — no open copy located (OhioLINK search form refused scripted queries; Kraal 2005 (ch. 3, p. 35, held by the project) summarizes it as treating penultimate lengthening as stress-driven and realized only utterance-finally, consistent with the phrasal coding. Also read held by the project: Leach 2010 §9.3.2 p. 330 (penultimate length marks the phonological-phrase boundary; confirms). Best new first-hand statement: Liphola 1991 pp. 31-32 and 115; it does not supersede Manus 2010 as the deciding source.

new_statements.quote: Em SMAK, o alongamento vocálico não é distintivo, uma vez que é predizível. A vogal longa, quando ocorre, tem quase sempre lugar na penúltima sílaba que antecede a pausa. Sua realização na língua é facultativa. Pelo contrário, o tom, a intensidade e os padrões tonais têm função distintiva. (pp. 31-32) [...] 1. O tom alto coincide sempre com o acento de intensidade. 2. A última sílaba (que antecede a pausa) não recebe tom, a menos que seja marcado no léxico. (p. 115)
new_statements.translation: In Si-Makonde, vowel lengthening is not distinctive, since it is predictable. The long vowel, when it occurs, almost always falls on the penultimate syllable preceding the pause. Its realization in the language is optional. By contrast, tone, stress and the tonal patterns have a distinctive function. [...] 1. High tone always coincides with stress. 2. The last syllable (preceding the pause) receives no tone unless it is lexically marked.
new_statements.citation: Liphola, Marcelino Marta. 1991. Tom, entonação e acento de intensidade na língua Si-Makonde: bases para um estudo morfotonológico. MA dissertation, IEL, Universidade Estadual de Campinas.
new_statements.locator: §3.2 'Vogal longa', pp. 31-32 (PDF pp. 45-46); §6.2 principle 1, p. 115 (PDF p. 131); conclusion p. 127 (PDF p. 144)
new_statements.reading: A native-speaker first-hand description that keeps the two candidate 'stress' correlates apart: predictable, optional penultimate lengthening before pause (a phrase/pause-level phenomenon, no length contrast) versus 'acento de intensidade', which Liphola equates with the H-toned syllable and therefore treats as lexically variable in position (first, second, penult or last syllable, p. 127). It confirms the pre-pausal penultimate-lengthening rule behind the catalog's 'phrasal' coding but does not support calling the penult the stressed syllable in the word-stress sense; under Liphola's terminology Makonde is a tone language whose prominence tracks H, with intonational penult lengthening at pause.

MA dissertation, Instituto de Estudos da Linguagem, Universidade Estadual de Campinas (advisor Maria Bernadete M. Abaurre). 156 pp. (scanned, scanned text layer).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: Mostramos que em SMAK tom alto e intensidade co-ocorrem e, dependendo do tipo de padrão tonal, a sílaba intensa (proeminente) pode ser a primeira, a segunda, a penúltima ou a última. Afirmamos, ainda, a existência de uma interdependência entre o tipo de estrutura fonológica e a ocorrência de tom alto e intensidade na primeira vogal do radical e no prefixo respectivo, enquanto que o alongamento vocálico (entonação) é ligado à posição de sílaba (preferencialmente a penúltima), sem valor contrastivo. (p. 127) — Translation: We showed that in Si-Makonde high tone and stress co-occur and that, depending on the tonal pattern, the stressed (prominent) syllable can be the first, the second, the penultimate or the last; ... whereas vowel lengthening (intonation) is tied to syllable position (preferably the penult), without contrastive value.
sources.locator: §3.2 'Vogal longa' pp. 31-32 (PDF pp. 45-46); rule p. 35; §6.2 'Princípios de correlação tom-sílaba' p. 115 (PDF p. 131); conclusion pp. 127-128 (PDF pp. 144-145)
sources.note: Native-speaker MA thesis. Separates three prosodic properties: tone (pitch), 'acento de intensidade' (stress = the most prominent syllable) and vowel lengthening (treated as intonational). (i) Vowel length is non-distinctive and predictable; the long vowel 'almost always' falls on the penultimate syllable before pause, its realization is optional ('facultativa'), and with CV+V+CV structures it can fall on the antepenult (pp. 31-35; rule p. 35: penult, or antepenult if V2 is long). (ii) Stress is identified with High tone: 'O tom alto coincide sempre com o acento de intensidade' (principle 1,…

sources.quote: p.63: 'there are no vowel length contrasts, but due to a regular stress rule, the penultimate syllable of every word is lengthened.' p.64: final syllable extraprosodic, 'stress is assigned to the final [visible, i.e. penultimate] syllable. Then, the stressed syllable is lengthened by (4) Stress Lengthening ... Stress with lengthening in utterance-medial words is not phonetically obvious, like utterance-final stress is, and is wiped out or severely reduced by a late postlexical rule.'

sources.citation: Leach, Michael Benjamin. 2010. Things hold together: foundations for a systemic treatment of verbal and nominal tone in Plateau Shimakonde. PhD dissertation, Universiteit Leiden (LOT 260). [Not a title-works with stress in the title; held by the project from the 2026-09-16 check; read here for the stress statement.]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: p.330: 'Penultimate length is assigned non-contrastively in Plateau Shimakonde to mark the boundary of the phonological phrase.' sec.9.5: 'Following previous descriptions of Makonde, we find that the phonological phrase is defined by penultimate lengthening and is the domain within which lexical and grammatical tone assignment takes place.' T9.19/T9.25: lengthening on verb and complement in disjoint constructions, only on the complement in conjoint ones.
sources.note: First-hand fieldwork description of Plateau Shimakonde (Mozambique). No length contrast (§2.1, p. 26); penultimate length is assigned non-contrastively to the penultimate syllable of the phonological phrase, making it bimoraic (§2.2, pp. 26-27; §9.3.2, p. 330); conjoint verbs before a complement lack it, disjoint verbs and complements both get it (T9.19); it applies even when H tone falls on the final syllable (T9.20). Leach does not use the word 'stress' for it. Confirms the catalog's phrasal coding (phrase-final penult lengthening).

sources.quote: Le makonde connaît un accent démarcatif réalisé comme un allongement de la pénultième devant pause absolue. Il n'y a pas dans cette langue d'opposition de longueur vocalique. (p. 358 n. 1) ... c) langues à culmination de longueur, mais non de hauteur, sur la pénultième (langues à prosodèmes distinctifs, mais sans opposition de longueur) : nande et konzo; langi; nyanja et chewa; makonde; ... (p. 484) — Translation: Makonde has a demarcative accent realized as lengthening of the penultimate before absolute pause. There is no vowel-length opposition in this language.
sources.locator: §3.9, pp. 357-359, footnote 1 on p. 358; typology ch. p. 484 with footnote 2 (TOC lists §3.9 at p. 351)
sources.note: Comparative thesis; §3.9 'Le makonde (dialecte maraba)' (pp. 357-359) is based on Odden's Chimaraba data and describes Makonde as 'une langue à accent, qui n'est pas sans rappeler le matuumbi', with three post-lexical strata of tone rules over prosodic groups. Footnote 1 (p. 358) states the stress fact directly: a demarcative accent realized as lengthening of the penultimate syllable before absolute pause; no vowel-length contrast. sources.quote: Like Odden, Liphola and Manus assume that penultimate lengthening takes place as the result of stress, and Liphola agrees with Odden that penultimate lengthening occurs in all words; only utterance-final lengthening is realized, and utterance-medially, the lengthening is wiped out. (Kraal 2005: 35, on Liphola 2001)

Not found on OhioLINK/OSU open pages.
